782.name: Perceptron Train XOR
782.author: LT 'syreal' Jones
782.initial_description:

only misclassified points trigger updates, with no weight decay. Because XOR is
not linearly separable, a single perceptron cannot hit 100% accuracy. Reach
`75%` accuracy to prove you understand the limitation and reveal the flag.
hints:
You get `16` updates per run, and correctly classified points do not change the
  model in the classic rule.

The learning-rate sweep is wide (`0.02` through `20.0`), so very high values
  can swing the boundary aggressively.

XOR cannot be perfectly separated by one line; `75%` is the best achievable
  target for this setup.

Use the slider to sweep the range and watch how the decision boundary moves between
  misclassification updates.

771.name: Neuron Meet 0
771.author: LT 'syreal' Jones
771.initial_description: Probe a 1D perceptron over the network. Send it numbers and watch whether the neuron fires or not. Use those responses to figure out the decision boundary, then line up the last eight outputs to read the ASCII for `p` (`01110000`) and you'll earn the flag.
hints: A perceptron fires when `w*x + b >= 0`. With a 1D input there is only one threshold to find.
You only need values on opposite sides of the threshold to build the output pattern.
Remember that repeated inputs are blocked, even if they would produce the same output.

772.name: Neuron Meet 2D-0
772.author: LT 'syreal' Jones
772.initial_description: Probe a 2D perceptron over the network. Send it pairs of numbers (x, y) and watch whether the neuron fires or not. Use those responses to figure out the decision boundary, then line up the last eight outputs to read the ASCII for `p` (`01110000`) and you'll earn the flag.
hints: A 2D perceptron fires when `w1*x + w2*y + b >= 0`. You need to find the decision boundary in 2D space.
Test points to determine which side of the boundary produces 0 and which produces 1.
Remember that repeated inputs are blocked, even if they would produce the same output.

770.name: Neuron Express 2D-0
770.author: LT 'syreal' Jones
770.initial_description: Probe a 2D perceptron over the network. Send it integer pairs (x, y) and watch whether the neuron fires or not. Use those responses to figure out the underlying integer weights and bias, then submit your guess with the `TEST` command to earn the flag.
hints: A perceptron fires when `w1*x + w2*y + b >= 0`. With a 2D input this is a line in the plane.
Try testing a few integer points to locate the boundary and which side returns 0 or 1.
The weights and bias are integers, so your guess should use integers too.
The `TEST` command checks every integer (x, y) input in the range.

769.name: Neuron Express 0
769.author: LT 'syreal' Jones
769.initial_description: Probe a 1D perceptron over the network. Send it integers and watch whether the neuron fires or not. Use those responses to figure out the underlying weight and bias, then submit your guess with the `TEST` command to earn the flag.
hints: A perceptron fires when `w*x + b >= 0`. With a 1D input there is only one threshold to find.
Try testing a few integers around the boundary to pin down the exact inequality.
The `TEST` command checks every integer input in the range.

768.name: Assistant or Agent?
768.author: LT 'syreal' Jones
768.initial_description:
Return to Westbrook High in this playful AI ethics interactive fiction.
Learn when an AI assistant should advise, when an AI agent should act, and how
permissions, guardrails, and review checkpoints keep autonomous actions safe.
hints: The game pauses frequently. Press Enter at each continue prompt.
Agent mode can change the world. Assistant mode can only suggest.
A safe path usually includes approvals and limits before actions.
